correctness.rationale: In column coordinates the equation is M^T x^[2]=x, so inversion and transposition give uniform A with x^[2]=Ax. The solution space is F_2-linear. A minimally field-dependent set of independent F_2-solutions would give a relation whose coefficients are unchanged by squaring, by subtracting the relations obtained from applying A and squaring coordinates. This contradicts F_2-independence and bounds the dimension by n. Every F_q independent k-frame has an equally independent squared frame; the number of matrices sending it to that frame is the group order divided by the number of frames, by transitivity. Thus all ordered fixed-frame moments equal 1, including k=0 and k=n. The resulting triangular system has diagonal |GL_k(F_2)|>0 and uniquely determines the same law as over F_2. Pointwise stabilizers of d-spaces have order 2^(d(n-d))|GL_(n-d)(F_2)|; subspace Möbius inversion gives the asserted formula. The no-idempotent probability tends to the binary Euler product by absolute convergence and expansion of that product. Independently enumerating binary matrices in dimensions 2 and 3 by testing bijectivity on all vectors gave exact histograms (2,3,1) and (48,98,21,1); the seven-letter derangement count from its recurrence is 1854. Dimension one has one nonzero idempotent. Conjecture 2's following limit statement does not restrict q to odd characteristic: its unrestricted-prime-power reading fails, not the characteristic-zero Galois-group assertion. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed.
